messages:
ana: seeing repeated 800-1200ms tails for small tenants on apac-rack-22 this morning. spikes line up with large write bursts to /var/checkpoints. :grimacing:
vik: any iostat or dmesg?
ana: quick paste:
```
iostat -x 1 2
Device: rrqm/s wrqm/s r/s w/s rkB/s wkB/s avgrq-sz avgqu-sz await r_await w_await svctm %util
nvme0n1 0.00 200.00 3.00 380.00  10.00  61440.00  160.00 12.00  19.0  2.0  40.0  2.0 98.0
```
```
[ 2345.678901] blk_update_request: I/O error, dev nvme0n1, sector 555555 op 1
```
maria: that looks like NVMe write saturation + retries. PCIe bandwidth also spikes per telemetry.
vik: quick mitigations:
- admission controller to enforce `redwood.io/blkio-bps` on new pods
- taint noisy pods and move to `io-isolated` nodes
- migrate heavy tenants to dedicated-pool if throttling continues
infra-bot: ALERT: pcie_bandwidth_util >85% on node gpu-apac-22 (auto-tagged).
ana: plan: canary on 2 nodes at 03:00 UTC tonight: apply blkio cap 40MB/s, tag top-5 writers, and monitor tail latency for 30m.
maria: prefer annotation-based enforcement, not sysfs echo. measure S3 fallback cost if we force uploads off-host.
vik: agreed. also add telemetry flag `checkpoint:heavy` to Optimize so it can suggest chunking and quieter upload cadence.
ana: ok will run canary and post results here. no objections?
maria: none. go ahead.
infra-bot: scheduled canary 3790001234-apac-io-cap at 2024-11-02T03:00:00Z (automated).
